sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle after completing a UChicago bachelor’s before entry; central GPA minimum 3.00 over last
60 semester hours (about 2 years), with program consideration below minimum possible. Math preparation
normally analysis I/II, algebra I/II, linear algebra and 4 advanced electives; graduate exposure common, not an
absolute requirement. No master’s needed. Actual GPA/course equivalence must be checked. International/F-1
applicants are eligible. [s5] [s6] [s2] [s4] [s12]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD/Fall 2027; arrange required Math GRE and official reporting; assemble transcripts,
20-course dossier, CV, two-page SOP and roughly 200-word background answer; request ≥3 faculty letters
early with Send to Recommender. For department fee grant, complete but do not submit application, stop at
Funding and Program Participation, email grad_program@math.wisc.edu by standing Dec 1 deadline. No
supervisor agreement required. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor required before applying; incoming academic adviser assigned, dissertation adviser selected by
end of the sixth semester. Faculty fit/contact is optional, capacity unconfirmed. Roster below focuses
continuing research faculty in requested fields, includes analytic NT/complex analysis adjacent matches;
postdocs/emeriti are not treated as guaranteed thesis advisers. Simon Marshall moved to Melbourne 2025;
Daniel Erman moved to Hawaii 2023; Ananth Shankar now at Northwestern - do not use old Wisconsin lists. [s6]
[s2] [f0] [fm1] [fm2] [fm3]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Application Portal shows status/decision/accept-decline. Submitted documents cannot be edited/replaced;
central says program may allow added documents, while Math FAQ says no updates, so finalize before

submission and ask about exceptions. Score matching begins only after submission and can take 3 weeks.
Referees managed separately. No account was opened or invitations sent. [s4] [s2]

Fall 2027 main page explicitly confirms required Math GRE and January 1 deadline; most detailed
portal/funding practices standing. 2027-28 stipend is university forecast, not Math offer. [s1] [s11]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
If not exempt: official TOEFL≥92 before 21 January 2026 or≥5.0 thereafter; IELTS/Indicator≥7; DET≥125;
scores under 2 years at enrollment. No combined/MyBest or IELTS One Skill Retake; TOEFL Home accepted.
Program-approved lower ranges TOEFL 80-91/4.5, IELTS 6.5, DET 115-124 require arrival ESLAT and assigned
ESL courses. TA spoken-English qualification is separate. [s5] [s4] [s16]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
Completed accredited US bachelor’s satisfies admission English requirement; alternatively≥2 full-time
semesters of graded exclusively English coursework within 5 years qualifies while degree is in progress (verify
quarter equivalence). No extra waiver essay published. TA policy exempts US bachelor’s recipients, but
departments may test those attending degree institution less than 4 full years. Math main page broadly says
non-native incoming students take SPEAK; request written confirmation of UChicago exception. [s5] [s17] [s16]
[s1]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional according to mathematics checklist; not required in Graduate Guide. This is distinct from mandatory
mathematics subject exam. [s1] [s6]
GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
REQUIRED for Fall 2027, official ETS report code 1846 by 1 January 2027. FAQ says GRE must be within 5 years
of matriculation in August. Department warns delivery may take 4 weeks; central matching takes 2-3 weeks
after submission, so arrange earlier than deadline. No published minimum score. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least 3 letters addressing mathematical promise, from mathematics faculty or other faculty able to judge
readiness for graduate mathematics. FAQ allows more than 3. Referees upload PDF directly through secure
system; Interfolio/file services not accepted. [s1] [s2] [s6] [s4]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Automatic departmental funding uses admission file; no extra scholarship referee or separate questionnaire
identified in admissions/funding instructions. Individual external or later-stage awards can differ. [s1] [s2] [s13]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Entering details alone is not the stated trigger: applicant clicks Send to Recommender; email contains secure
upload directions. Name, email, phone and optional personalized message requested. [s4]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Requests can be sent before submission and remain accessible afterward. After submit/payment applicant can
add/exclude referees and send reminders; pending letters still due January 1. [s4] [s1]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Email confirmation when uploaded; after submission Status Page/Application Checklist shows received versus
missing. [s4] [s2]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Letters do not carry over between separate program applications; referee must upload anew. Replacing an
already submitted letter and reuse across years are not publicly documented. Applicant can
add/exclude/remind after submission. Contact admissions@grad.wisc.edu for referee technical issues. [s4]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required PDF CV/resume. Prompt paraphrase: education, teaching/research experience, publications and
accomplishments. No public page/word/font/spacing cap; linked example is illustrative, not a verified
formatting mandate. Upload document rather than link. [s1] [s6] [s3]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required PDF, maximum 2 pages. Faithful prompt paraphrase: why study mathematics at UW; research
interests, career goals, and preparation, including coursework, work, research, publications, presentations,

awards, honors. No font/margin/spacing rule published. Central guidance encourages specific program/faculty
fit and brief explanation of anomalies. [s6] [s1] [s8]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Required supplemental background response, about 200 words (approximate target, not publicly stated hard
maximum). Faithful paraphrase: explain how personal background and geographic, financial, educational or
other opportunities/challenges motivated graduate study at UW. Appears as supplemental question; public
page does not establish separate PDF versus text-box implementation, font, or character cap. [s3]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Include in SOP and select best-fit field plus all relevant research areas in supplement; these choices are not
binding. No separate research-interest essay listed. Best-fit choices include Algebra, Analysis,
Applied/Computational Math, Differential Equations, Dynamics, Geometry/Topology, Logic, Probability, Broad
Interests. Multi-select includes AG, NT, representation theory and complex analysis. [s3] [s6]
Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
Not listed as a separate required admissions document in math checklist or Graduate Guide. Optional
proposal/thesis/sample uploading or linking permission, limits and format are not established; ask before
attaching unsolicited papers. [s1] [s6]
Publications list [Standing rule]
Include publications in CV and relevant preparation in SOP; no separate publications-list or paper-PDF
requirement listed. Rules for optional paper uploads/links not public. [s6] [s1]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Required PDF 20-course list/table described in course_list; description~50 words each. Sample linked publicly;
no total page/font cap specified. [s3]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
No additional admissions essay for automatic math funding. Department fee grant uses completed but
unsubmitted application and request email; no separate essay limit published. External fellowships have
separate prompts and may restrict citizenship. [s1] [s2] [s13]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Supplement also asks undergraduate institution type (UChicago reasonably private research university),
whether graduate courses were offered, master’s-degree status, native English, and whether 4 years
secondary education were exclusively English. Other research area allows explanatory text. No extra length
limit public. [s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
Official FY 2026-27 Math rate sheet, 50% appointment: TA academic-year gross USD 30,614; PA/RA
academic-year 31,306; PA/RA annual 37,417. University forecast explicitly sets 2027-28 annualized 50%
minimum 39,288, not a math 12-month offer. Its A-to-C conversion is 9/11; arithmetic academic
minimum≈32,144.73, pending official 2027 rate confirmation. Summer cash guarantee not established. Tuition
remission excludes segregated fees, international student fee, and one-time official document fee (current
130). Health coverage available with employee premiums; not full premium-free guarantee. [s10] [s11] [s9] [s1]
[s15]
Years of support [Standing rule]
All admitted PhD students offered support, usually TA, guaranteed 5 years subject to satisfactory progress.
Department tries to fund later years if research and teaching satisfactory, not a sixth-year guarantee. Public
page does not define annual summer duration; obtain offer’s calendar coverage. [s1] [s2]

International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students eligible for assistantships, University Fellowships and some departmental fellowships.
All-admit math support statement has no nationality exclusion. F-1 work authorization/SEVIS transfer is
separate and should be handled with ISS after admission. [s12] [s1]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Satisfactory academic/research progress and teaching performance; TA support requires spoken-English
competence, with support during prescribed improvement under L&S policy. Tuition remission normally ≥33%
appointment. Assistantship health plan has premiums; excluded fees remain student responsibility.
Department does not require teaching as a degree requirement, but accepting TA entails assigned duties. [s1]
[s9] [s17]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No extra TA/RA form with admission; all available departmental support considered automatically. RAs usually
later through adviser/grant; no separate entrance RA application. External awards independent. [s1] [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
University/department fellowships and later adviser RA; central external-fellowship search databases and
Funding Forward workshops. University Fellowships can nominate international students. NSF GRFP and other
citizenship-limited schemes should not be assumed eligible for F-1 applicant. Summer page gives
enrollment/benefit logistics but no universal summer stipend commitment. [s12] [s13] [s14] [s2]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75 nonrefundable application fee plus USD 6 international processing=USD 81. One fee covers up to 3
programs in same entry term; separate applications and new referee uploads needed. MasterCard/Visa/debit
accepted. [s4]
Fee waiver [Conflict]
Central fee grant is restricted to US citizens/permanent residents, so F-1 applicant ineligible. Program grants
have no central citizenship bar; Math asks completed-unsubmitted application then email
grad_program@math.wisc.edu by December 1, decision December 10 (standing dates/year unspecified).
Central site presently suspends NEW program fee grant purchases due to Workday transition; this does not
prove existing math codes unavailable. Confirm availability before paying; no refunds. Central qualifying
applicants need ≥5 business days and documentation, but that route does not apply here. USD 6 coverage not
established. [s4] [s7] [s2]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle after completing a UChicago bachelor’s before entry; central GPA minimum 3.00 over last
60 semester hours (about 2 years), with program consideration below minimum possible. Math preparation
normally analysis I/II, algebra I/II, linear algebra and 4 advanced electives; graduate exposure common, not an
absolute requirement. No master’s needed. Actual GPA/course equivalence must be checked. International/F-1
applicants are eligible. [s5] [s6] [s2] [s4] [s12]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD/Fall 2027; arrange required Math GRE and official reporting; assemble transcripts,
20-course dossier, CV, two-page SOP and roughly 200-word background answer; request ≥3 faculty letters
early with Send to Recommender. For department fee grant, complete but do not submit application, stop at
Funding and Program Participation, email grad_program@math.wisc.edu by standing Dec 1 deadline. No
supervisor agreement required. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor required before applying; incoming academic adviser assigned, dissertation adviser selected by
end of the sixth semester. Faculty fit/contact is optional, capacity unconfirmed. Roster below focuses
continuing research faculty in requested fields, includes analytic NT/complex analysis adjacent matches;
postdocs/emeriti are not treated as guaranteed thesis advisers. Simon Marshall moved to Melbourne 2025;
Daniel Erman moved to Hawaii 2023; Ananth Shankar now at Northwestern - do not use old Wisconsin lists. [s6]

Pay attention to
• Fall 2027 specifically REQUIRES Math GRE; application and every supporting item due 1 January 2027,

• UChicago admission-English exemption does not by itself resolve the math page’s blanket SPEAK language;

fee, document fee and employee health premiums can remain payable.

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle after completing a UChicago bachelor’s before entry; central GPA minimum 3.00 over last
60 semester hours (about 2 years), with program consideration below minimum possible. Math preparation
normally analysis I/II, algebra I/II, linear algebra and 4 advanced electives; graduate exposure common, not an
absolute requirement. No master’s needed. Actual GPA/course equivalence must be checked. International/F-1
applicants are eligible. [s5] [s6] [s2] [s4] [s12]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD/Fall 2027; arrange required Math GRE and official reporting; assemble transcripts,
20-course dossier, CV, two-page SOP and roughly 200-word background answer; request ≥3 faculty letters
early with Send to Recommender. For department fee grant, complete but do not submit application, stop at
Funding and Program Participation, email grad_program@math.wisc.edu by standing Dec 1 deadline. No
supervisor agreement required. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor required before applying; incoming academic adviser assigned, dissertation adviser selected by
end of the sixth semester. Faculty fit/contact is optional, capacity unconfirmed. Roster below focuses
continuing research faculty in requested fields, includes analytic NT/complex analysis adjacent matches;
postdocs/emeriti are not treated as guaranteed thesis advisers. Simon Marshall moved to Melbourne 2025;
Daniel Erman moved to Hawaii 2023; Ananth Shankar now at Northwestern - do not use old Wisconsin lists. [s6]
